summary: Iteration 2 testing (backend + frontend). Backend: 16/16 pytest cases pass — IRR compute, cash flow add/remove, investment PATCH, company PATCH persistence, LP CSV export, Dealroom CSV import (create + re-import updates). Frontend: Dashboard shows all 5 metrics (Deployed/DryPowder/MOIC/IRR/Investments), IRR displays '—' with 'add cash flows' subtext, LP export URL returns 200 text/csv with correct headers, Companies page has Import Dealroom button + dialog, real-time search filter, and pagination (prev/next). Company detail inline edit WORKS functionally (PATCH persists) but the read-state clickable elements have the WRONG data-testid: 'edit-edit-sector' etc. instead of the spec-required 'edit-sector' (double prefix from EditableField). The 'edit-sector' testid is only on the inner <input> when editing.

ui_bugs.issue: Read-state clickable button uses data-testid=`edit-{testid}` while parent already passes testid=`edit-sector`, yielding `edit-edit-sector` etc. Spec expects 'edit-sector','edit-round','edit-ask','edit-hq','edit-website','edit-lead','edit-source' on the clickable field.

action_items: Fix EditableField in /app/frontend/src/pages/CompanyDetail.jsx line 210: change `data-testid={`edit-${testid}`}` to `data-testid={testid}` so read-state button matches spec (edit-sector, edit-round, edit-ask, edit-hq, edit-website, edit-lead, edit-source). The input already uses `data-testid={testid}` which will conflict — either give input a separate id like `${testid}-input` or rely on only one being in DOM at a time (currently only one is rendered based on `editing` state, so single testid works).

rca of the issue: In CompanyDetail.jsx EditableField, the read-state <button> uses data-testid `edit-${testid}`. Since callers already pass testid='edit-sector', the resulting attribute becomes 'edit-edit-sector'. The intended interpretation of the spec is that the clickable field itself carries the 'edit-*' testid. Fix: change `data-testid={`edit-${testid}`}` to `data-testid={testid}` on the button (line 210). This is a HIGH priority spec-conformance bug (functionality works but automated tests using spec selectors would fail).
